gaps.text: In-line measurement of Temperature at the measurement point with temperature sensor

Combining several spectroscopy methods (data fusion) (Fusion level: start with one model per method and then join the NIR and Raman blocks with block scaling, since variables from different methods are not equivalent. Both techniques must look at the same small area of the same granulate stream, and the two data streams must be normalised to a common time step, with each instrument keeping its own calibration and diagnostics. The fused model must beat the best single method on independent batches, otherwise the second instrument is dropped.)
An accuracy or precision figure for moisture in a granulate or any comparable solid, so the plus or minus 0.1 % requirement cannot be confirmed from the supplied pages.
Regulatory approval or qualification for release testing.

items.finding: The temperature sensitivity of OH bands in NIR and MIR is described as a severe drawback for measuring aqueous solutions, making tempered sample holders necessary.
items.how_it_applies: For moisture measurement, temperature at the measurement point may affect the OH bands, so temperature monitoring or control at the granulate stream could be considered when assessing O2.
items.limits_and_transfer_risks: The statement concerns aqueous solutions and tempered sample holders, not in-line temperature measurement in a granulate stream; transfer to a solid granulate matrix and to an industrial measurement point is not established.

citation.quote: Additionally, the temperature sensitivity of the OH bands is a severe drawback for measuring aqueous solution in NIR and MIR, which makes tempered sample holders necessary [29].
citation.label: E02 ¶12

items.finding: Before fusing data from multiple sources, the contribution of each dataset and its complementarity should be evaluated.
items.how_it_applies: This supports testing whether Raman adds complementary information to NIR before keeping the second instrument, and dropping it if the fused model does not improve on the best single method.
items.limits_and_transfer_risks: This is a general PAT data-fusion review statement, not a NIR-plus-Raman granulate study; complementarity can differ with sample, matrix, and process conditions.

citation.quote: Before fusing data from multiple sources, it is essential to evaluate the contribution of each dataset to the model and its complementarity.
citation.label: E03 ¶82

items.finding: In a cartilage-health study, concatenating Raman, MIR, and NIR spectra in a multi-block fusion gave higher classification accuracy than single-block models, with PCA-SVM fusion at 81% and multiblock PLS-DA at 79.1%.
items.how_it_applies: This is a reason to test a fused NIR and Raman model against the best single method on independent batches, as required for O3, rather than assuming fusion will help.
items.limits_and_transfer_risks: The result is from ex vivo cartilage classification, not moisture in granulate; the modalities, sample type, and prediction target differ, so the reported improvement may not transfer.

citation.quote: For multi-block (fusion) approach of concatenating all three spectral modalities, PCA-SVM fusion achieved the highest accuracy of 81%, and multiblock PLS-DA attained 79.1%, both significantly better than the single-block models as confirmed via analysis of variance, highlighting the benefit of multimodal spectral integration for assessing cartilage health.
citation.label: E05 ¶23
